Set a valid interval. Minutes and seconds must be between 0 and 59.
Check start/stop durations and acquisition limit.
For more reliable automatic acquisition while the screen is off, allow Uvir to use the battery without restrictions. The session may still stop if the app is force-closed.
Unable to stop automatic acquisition. Check the sensor connection and try again.
Stop the current automatic acquisition. Continue?
Connect the sensor to change these settings.
Configure the general aspects of the sensor.
Connect a sensor to acquire data, record alerts, or change its settings.
Open Settings › Sensor › Connection to choose USB, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or Internet and view the instructions.
To use Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, connect the sensor by USB at least once. The app will securely acquire the sensor’s unique identity and access credentials.
The app connects remotely to the sensor through a secure MQTT broker. No router port needs to be opened. App and sensor connect outward, so this also works with mobile routers and CGNAT.
Keeps the sensor reachable through the configured MQTT broker.
Uses the network already configured in the Wi-Fi section.
Host name only: no protocol, port or path.
You can change this setting by USB or through the other active wireless connection. If both radios are disabled, USB is required to re-enable one.
Sensor not connected. Use USB, Wi-Fi or Bluetooth and try again.
Default and priority connection when the cable is inserted.
Mock data is active. To select a sensor, disable it.
A disabled source can be re-enabled through the other active wireless connection. If both are disabled, connect the sensor by USB.

The sensor enters a low-power shutdown and cannot be restarted from the app. To turn it on again, press EN/RESET or disconnect and reconnect its power. To confirm, press and hold POWER OFF for 5 seconds.

Dissociating removes the sensor from the selectable list, without deleting its name or saved records. You can associate it again by USB at any time. The sensor remains unchanged. To confirm, press and hold DISSOCIATE for 5 seconds.
Could not change sensor. Try again.
Connect the new sensor by USB. Previously associated sensors remain in the list.

Restore all app and sensor settings to their defaults and permanently delete all saved acquisitions, recorded alerts and error logs. The sensor powers off afterwards. To confirm, press and hold RESTORE ALL continuously for 10 seconds.
The complete restore could not be performed. Check the sensor connection and try again.

Delete all Uvir app settings and locally stored data, including acquisitions, recorded alerts, error logs, counters, sensor profiles and saved connection credentials. The sensor itself is not changed or powered off. To confirm, press and hold RESET for 5 seconds.
The app could not be reset.
The app communicates with the sensor when both use the same Wi-Fi network.
You can save or change wireless networks over USB or through an already active and authenticated wireless connection. If no wireless connection is available, use USB.
Pair the sensor from Android Bluetooth settings; its connection to the app is direct and authenticated.
VIS/NIR values are estimates in µW/cm² derived from typical AS7343 datasheet responsivity. Absolute calibration of this physical module still requires a calibrated optical reference.
Connect the sensor once by USB to securely obtain its unique name and access credentials.
Android does not allow apps to read a saved Wi-Fi password. Enter it only the first time: it is stored privately and is never exposed by the sensor over wireless connections.
Wi-Fi network saved to the sensor
Sensor not connected. Use USB, Wi-Fi or Bluetooth and try again
Sampling is performed directly inside the sensor: the app receives only the processed final result.
Extreme-value trimming removes the highest and lowest samples and requires at least 3 samples.
When the interval is below 500 ms, the Live screen refreshes values every 500 ms while still processing every received sample.
Use 1–21 samples and a spacing between 150 and 5000 ms.
Use the bell on each group on the main screen to configure values and limits. Here you can choose the alert sound.
Triggers when the value is equal to or above the limit.
Triggers when the value is equal to or below the limit.
Final loudness also depends on the phone’s alarm volume.
Use non-negative limits and set a repeat interval between 1 second and 24 hours.
End the current alert session. Configured and recorded alerts are kept.
Start monitoring using the configured alerts. You can add or remove alerts during the session.
Reset all active alerts. To confirm, press and hold RESET ALL continuously for 2 seconds.
One or more active alerts in this group
%1$s is above the limit. Current value %2$.1f. Limit %3$.1f.
%1$s is below the limit. Current value %2$.1f. Limit %3$.1f.
Permanently delete all recorded alerts. To confirm, press and hold DELETE ALL continuously for 2 seconds.
Manage the reset of counters and their associated data.
Export or manage stored data and counters, or reset the app and sensor to their default state.
Manage exports, imports and reset options.
Reset all counters, the sensor or the app.
Deletes all app and sensor data, restores the default settings, then powers off the sensor.
Deletes every setting and all data stored in the app. The sensor and the data still stored on it remain unchanged.
Deletes unsynchronized data stored on the sensor, resets its configuration and connection credentials, then powers it off.

Reset only the sensor. Its settings and connection credentials return to their defaults; unsynchronized acquisitions, alerts and errors stored on it are deleted, then the sensor powers off. App settings and records already saved in Uvir remain unchanged. To confirm, press and hold RESET for 5 seconds.
The sensor could not be reset. Check the connection and try again.
Deletes all saved acquisitions and recorded alerts, then resets their IDs and session IDs.
Permanently delete all saved acquisitions and recorded alerts. Their IDs and session IDs restart from the beginning. To confirm, press and hold RESET ALL continuously for 5 seconds.
Permanently deletes all saved acquisitions and resets acquisition and session IDs.
Permanently delete all saved acquisitions and reset acquisition and session IDs. The alert log and alert settings remain unchanged. To confirm, press and hold RESET ALL continuously for 2 seconds.
Permanently deletes all recorded alerts and resets alert IDs.
Permanently delete all recorded alerts and reset alert IDs. Saved acquisitions and alert settings remain unchanged. To confirm, press and hold RESET ALL continuously for 2 seconds.
Stop automatic acquisition before resetting the counters.
Export/import app and sensor settings with encrypted backups.
Export/restore the complete database with an encrypted ZIP backup.
Replace the records and sensor profiles on this phone with those in the backup. The physical sensor remains unchanged. Enter the ZIP password to continue.
Unable to import the database. Check the password, archive and database version.
¹ Experimental broad-band estimates derived from the acquired channels. They are not medical, diagnostic, or safety assessments. The model will be refined after real-sensor calibration.
Estimated equivalent UV irradiance weighted for potential DNA effects: higher values mean greater spectrally relevant exposure. Percentage of total UV.
Estimated equivalent UV irradiance weighted for potential photoaging: higher values mean greater spectrally relevant exposure. Percentage of total UV.
Estimated equivalent HEV irradiance (violet + blue) associated with potential oxidative stress: higher values mean greater relevant exposure. Percentage of visible light.

0–100 shows how strongly the acquired spectrum is concentrated in wavelengths weighted by this estimate. It describes spectral composition, not total intensity. It is not a percentage of damage and not a safety threshold.
Permanently delete all saved acquisitions. To confirm, press and hold DELETE ALL continuously for 2 seconds.
¹ High Energy Visible (high-energy visible light): the sum of the violet and blue components.
¹ Bandwidth at half maximum: about 60 nm (Far-red) and 54 nm (NIR).
App and sensor links work; development is on hold pending optical validation.
The lid and apertures are theoretical prototypes, not validated measurement optics.
Calibration tools include mean offsets, adaptive UV gain and guided window factors.
Smoother Main View expansion; saved-view choices last for the current app session.
Reliable absolute measurements still require final optics and reference calibration.
Spectral acquisition app for ultraviolet, visible and infrared radiation.
Spectral bands: Ultraviolet • Visible light • Infrared
Supported sensors: AS7331 UV • AS7343 multispectral
Estimated biological effects are derived values calculated from acquired spectral data.

Connect the cable, open Uvir and choose USB in the desktop program.
The phone and computer must be connected to the same private Wi-Fi network. Copy the address and code shown here into the desktop program.
Wi-Fi address not detected. Connect the phone to a Wi-Fi network.
1. Open Settings → Connections.\n2. Open Mobile Hotspot and Tethering.\n3. Enable Bluetooth tethering.
1. Open Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Devices.\n2. Expand the phone and select Join next to Personal Area Network.\n3. Choose Access Point and select Connect.
Bluetooth address not detected. Enable Bluetooth tethering; this screen refreshes automatically.
Use this section when the phone is connected through its own mobile data connection, outside the Wi-Fi network.
Mobile network address not detected. Enable mobile data on the phone.
Other detected address: %1$s — Android cannot identify its type.
For access away from home, preferably use a private VPN. Router port forwarding concerns the home connection’s public address, not the mobile addresses shown here.
The connection is not active yet. Allow local network access when Android requests it.
Use direct access only on a trusted private network. The pairing code is required for every direct connection.
Local network permission denied. Direct Wi-Fi and Bluetooth access remains disabled.
The sensor memory was full. Autonomous recording was stopped to protect existing data.
The sensor still contains data that could not be synchronized. Keep it connected and try again.
Sensor disconnection, offline autonomy, and synchronization updates.
Sensor not connected. Offline recording continues within the available memory.
Sensor memory is full. Offline recording cannot start.
Conservative estimate: simultaneous threshold violations use one alert record per repeat interval.
The sensor connection was lost. This estimate combines the active automatic acquisition and alerts.
Offline autonomous recording is disabled. The sensor does not store new acquisitions or alerts while disconnected.
The latest sensor status does not contain enough information to estimate the remaining autonomy.
When the phone is unreachable, the sensor stores completed acquisitions and alerts locally and synchronizes them after reconnection.
When no operation or synchronization is active and the app remains disconnected, the sensor enters low-power shutdown after the selected time. It must then be reactivated physically.
Uses the LEDs for status signals.
Sensor disconnected with activity in progress.
Sensor connected with activity in progress.
Data in memory waiting to be synchronized.
Alerts remain active, but no events are saved on the sensor or in the app.
Uses the buzzer for status signals.
Start of an automatic acquisition or alert session.
End of an automatic acquisition or alert session.
Connect the sensor to change the alert interval.
Connect the sensor to change these alerts.
This interval is stored in the sensor and also limits alerts recorded while the app is disconnected.
Adjust correction factors and offsets for each channel.
Correction factors: allowed values %1$s–%2$s; %3$s leaves the gain unchanged. Determine them using a calibrated reference instrument.
Update the sensor firmware to use calibration.
The firmware installed on the sensor does not support these settings. Update the sensor firmware and try again.
Value outside the allowed limits. It was corrected automatically.
Name shown only in this app. The sensor’s hardware ID does not change.

An acquisition is saved only when the sensor detects a command on the external input. The session note is retained; interval, scheduled start, end, maximum count and acquisition conditions are ignored.
Set the values and thresholds for acquisition. Conditions are copied to the sensor when the session starts.
Configure at least one condition before starting.
Three short beeps in a row
Acquisition not recorded: date and time unavailable.
Checks every sample. When the condition is met, collection starts immediately and the acquisition interval begins.
Checks every sample, including between acquisitions. Stops immediately when the condition is met.
Collects a measurement as soon as the condition is met. After saving, pauses condition checks for the full interval, then resumes.
The initial delay, duration and maximum acquisition count always take priority. Measurements retain the configured sampling.
No records are selected. Share all records matching the current filters.
Choose how data is displayed and formatted in the app.
Choose the unit used to display irradiance. Stored sensor values keep their original precision.
Choose the feedback played by the app when a manual or automatic acquisition is saved.
Final loudness also depends on the phone’s alarm volume.
Choose the feedback played by the app when a alert is recorded.
No records are selected. Export all records matching the current filters.
Includes connection credentials and the sensor association, allowing it to be restored without USB. Requires an encryption password.
Use at least 8 characters. Use the same password to import the backup later.
This backup is encrypted. Enter the password used when it was exported.
Shows how the sensor responds to commands received on the external input.
Uses the external input to acquire data and control sessions. Requires a valid date and time on the sensor.
Saves a standalone acquisition or the next acquisition in an active external session.
Starts an external session. The three presses themselves do not save acquisitions.
Stops the active acquisition or alert session.
A triple press is ignored. Short presses save only when the active session is external.
Nothing is recorded or started; the RGB LED flashes red rapidly five times and the buzzer emits one prolonged beep.
Treat a group of acquisitions as variants of the same measurement (for example, different angles).
Each variant is displayed and exported as a separate group, which may increase the number of generated files.
Press and hold %1$s for %2$d seconds to confirm.
Configure at least one value before starting.
Replace the current settings with those contained in the selected files.
